reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound: extending dwell time at high temperature increases atomic mobility, which can allow a kinetically trapped solid solution to evolve toward equilibrium phases (segregation or ordering), consistent with diffusion kinetics and thermodynamics.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive: systematically varying dwell time and using XRD/STEM-EDX to detect phase separation or ordering, with a well-defined falsification criterion (no change from baseline).
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a central challenge in HEA nanoparticle synthesis (kinetic trapping vs. thermodynamic stability) and provides a straightforward, controllable intervention that would yield mechanistic insight into phase selection.
